newsitem.title: ITALY: Banco Napoli control passes to INA, BNL.
newsitem.headline: Banco Napoli control passes to INA, BNL.

text.p: Control of troubled Italian bank Banco di Napoli officially passed to insurance company INA and banking group BNL on Wednesday, the Italian Treasury said.

"An important phase in the process of cleaning up and privatising Banco di Napoli has ended with a solution which exceeds the rescue aim and which opens a phase of strengthening and development," the Treasury said in a statement.

Newly formed Banco di Napoli Holding Spa, which is 51 percent owned by INA and 49 percent by Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, took over a 60 percent stake sold by the Treasury as part of a project to rescue the southern Italian bank.

The 61.7 billion lire ($36.5 million) deal, which is equal to 45 lire per share, was worked out earlier this year to shore up the loss-making bank and leaves 39 percent of its capital still in the Treasury's hands.
The Treasury said in a statement however it meant to sell the reminder as soon as market conditions permitted.

INA, which is 34.3 percent controlled by the state, and BNL, which is owned by the Treasury, created Banco di Napoli Holding to acquire the 60 percent stake, equivalent to 1.37 billion Banco di Napoli shares.

The purchase was part of a rescue plan worked out after the bank clocked up a cumulative 5.797 trillion lire of losses between 1994 and 1996. INA said recently it expects the bank to break even this year.

A statement from INA said the board of Banco di Napoli Holding Spa had already decided to call an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve increasing its capital to one trillion lire from the current 100 billion.
In addition it said the Treasury would have two representatives on the bank's board until the ministry's stake fell to 10 percent of the ordinary share capital. $1=1,692 lire
